topic: Lambda Init Capture for Moving Resource-Owning Objects
explanation: Assumption: Standard capture modes (`[=]` or `[&]`) are sufficient for all scenarios, and `std::move` can be used inside the capture list to move resources into the closure. Reality: Prior to C++14, it was impossible to move objects (especially move-only types like `std::unique_ptr` or `std::thread`) into a lambda closure because capture by value requires copying, and capture by reference creates dangling references if the lambda outlives the scope. Init capture (C++14 generalized capture) provides the syntax `[name = initial_expression]` which allows the creation of a new data member in the closure initialized by the expression. Why It Fails: Init capture is necessary to move resource-owning objects. The expression `[ptr = std::move(p)]` moves the resource `p` into the closure's data member `ptr`, ensuring the closure owns the resource and preventing copies.
practical_example: A developer needs a lambda to manage a temporary file handle represented by a move-only type. Without init capture, they cannot safely pass ownership of the handle into the lambda body.
keywords: Init capture, Move lambda capture, C++14 generalized capture, unique_ptr lambda
chapter: Item 32: Use init capture to move objects into closures
